newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas still down late but holds support.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas still down late but holds support.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained mostly lower late Monday in moderate trade, but prices, helped by a firmer cash, were still holding above technical support, industry sources said.
At 1415 EDT, June was down 5.9 cents at $2.19 per million British thermal units, while July was 3.5 cents lower at $2.23. Most others were down by one-half to 3.5 cents.

"It seems like prices are well-handicapped at current levels, but I think we're building a bias for more rallies," said one New York-based futures trader, noting good buying in June in the high-teens and selling near $2.30.

While forecasts this week for normal to slightly below-normal weather for most of the nation may favor the bears, bulls point to steady injection demand and some heat in the Southwest as offsetting factors. In addition, they said the likelihood of better cooling demand later in the month should temper any selling.
Technical traders agreed the market was range-bound, with the broader range for June between the $2.05 double bottom and the $2.43 contract high.
Maintenance on Transco's Texas line will continue to cut about 400 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) out of a total capacity of about 600 mmcfd Tuesday through Thursday.

In the cash, Gulf Coast swing prices firmed about a nickel Monday to the low-$2.20s. Midcon pipes were up a similar amount to the low-$2s. New York city gate gas was quoted more than five cents higher at about $2.50.
NYMEX said 29,072 contracts traded at 1345 EDT.
On KCBT, June was still down by 1.1 cents at $2.06, while deferreds remained steady to two cents lower. The East/West spread narrowed by 4.8 cents to 13.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
